- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Write control markers under a dedicated watchdog identity" (linked issue #5135, recommendation).
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/claude-issue-queue-watchdog.yml (the GH_TOKEN binding, line 39) plus the supporting script and docs.
  Evidence of absence: The PR description, plan, README, and agents.md all describe the binding as "the watchdog's GH_PAT" / "its GH_PAT" / "the account the watchdog posts with (its GH_PAT)". The actual binding at .github/workflows/claude-issue-queue-watchdog.yml:39 is `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` — the default GitHub Actions installation token, not secrets.GH_PAT. The PR's pr_changed_files list does not include .github/workflows/claude-issue-queue-watchdog.yml, and a grep across the repo shows this workflow is the only one in the entire repository that uses the bare `github.token` form; every other workflow that needs to author comments and read its own identity (review_autofix.yml line 706, orchestrate.yml line 100, validate.yml, security-audit.yml, memory_maintenance.yml, etc.) uses `secrets.GH_PAT` or the `secrets.GH_PAT || github.token` fallback. The new `gh api user` call in scripts/claude_issue_queue_watchdog.sh therefore resolves the GitHub Actions app identity, not a dedicated watchdog account. The PR description's claim that the binding is to GH_PAT is not implemented; the recommendation's "dedicated watchdog identity" requirement is not met.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "verify their author and dispatch provenance" (linked issue #5135, recommendation).
  Expected change site: scripts/claude_issue_route.py env_requeue_decision marker loop (around the new login check) and scripts/claude_issue_queue_watchdog.sh marker posting.
  Evidence of absence: The new check at scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1120 compares only each comment's `user.login` to the resolved `watchdog_login`. It does not verify that a marker was produced by a specific watchdog workflow run. The plan's AD-3 explicitly chose to reject the dispatch-provenance check, on the reasoning that "only the `GH_PAT` account can pass the author check, and that account can already send the dispatch itself, so B narrows no attacker class". That reasoning depends on the binding being to GH_PAT (a specific personal access token, used only by the watchdog script). The actual binding is to whatever identity the default GitHub Actions token authenticates as, which is shared by every workflow run on the repository that uses `github.token`. Any other workflow on this repository can therefore post comments with the same author identity, and the provenance check would meaningfully narrow the attacker class. The plan's AD-3 reasoning is invalid for the implementation as shipped, and the linked issue's "verify their author and dispatch provenance" recommendation is unmet.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "The watchdog resolves its login from the token it posts with (gh api user --jq .login, one REST call per env-requeue run) and passes it to env-requeue-plan --watchdog-login <login>." (plan, Goals section).
  Expected change site: scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1117-1118 and the dispatch site in scripts/claude_issue_queue_watchdog.sh.
  Evidence of absence: The check at scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1120 compares `_user_field(comment, "login").casefold()` to `watchdog_key`. Comments posted with `github.token` are attributed to `github-actions[bot]` (TRUSTED_ISSUE_BOT_AUTHOR at scripts/claude_issue_route.py:144). For an installation token, `GET /user` returns the user identity of the installation owner rather than the bot identity that the token posts as. The workflow at .github/workflows/claude-issue-queue-watchdog.yml:39 does not pass `secrets.GH_PAT` to GH_TOKEN, so the resolved `watchdog_login` will not match `github-actions[bot]`. The result is that every legitimate watchdog marker is filtered out by the `continue` at scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1120-1122: the decision sees zero re-queue / exhausted markers from the watchdog's own identity, the cap never reaches `alert`, and the env-requeue step becomes a no-op for every previously-re-queued or alerted issue. The fail-closed guard at the call site (`warn env_requeue_skipped reason=watchdog_login_unknown` when `gh api user` fails) is fine on its own; the runtime failure mode is the steady-state path where the lookup succeeds but returns the wrong class of identity. The PR's test suite passes because the test stub (`tests/test_claude_issue_route.py:2123` and the env_stubs gh stub) hard-codes the resolved login to `shubhodeep1` and the test comment author to `shubhodeep1`; production uses `github-actions[bot]` for the comment and a different login for the lookup. Fix: either (a) update .github/workflows/claude-issue-queue-watchdog.yml:39 to `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT || github.token }}` and have the matching script step post the marker with that token, or (b) accept the GitHub Actions bot as a valid identity when the resolved login is one of the install-token app identities, or (c) post the markers through a different mechanism whose author identity is provably the resolved one. The new docs and the changelog fragment already describe the GH_PAT binding, so option (a) is the smallest change that makes the docs match the code.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
